new_statements.second_reader_evidence: .., 18-pp scan, no text layer) at 100 dpi myself and also viewed the saved 200-dpi crop. In pencil, directly above the left-hand column headed 'Date: 14 Nov. 2007 / Language: Borogo na Tabaruma / Village: Waderi / State: Niger / Informant: Habubacar Bawa / Age 22 Sex M / Elicited by: MRueck', the note reads 'stress on 2nd syl. / length, volume' followed by a check mark; left margin also has 'elicited in (H)' [= Hausa]. The right-hand column (Tucindi, Dan Asabe, 15 Nov 2007, Mike Rueck) has informant names above it, not the stress note, so the note's position ties it to the Waderi/Borogo elicitation. Quote is verbatim (the '/' in the report marks the line break). The transcriptions themselve…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The SIL surveyor eliciting the 355-item wordlist from a Rogo (Shiyabe) speaker noted that word stress falls on the second syllable, realised as greater length and loudness. This is a field impression jotted on the wordlist form, not an analysis; since Kamuku nouns are cited with a CV/V noun-class prefix (bɔ-, tu-, u-, a-...), 'second syllable' in citation forms will very often be the root-initial syllable, and the language cluster is otherwise described as tonal (two level tones in closely related Cinda).
new_statements.exceptions: none; the note is a single line
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms elicited for a survey wordlist (words said in isolation; Yoder et al. 2014 sec. 3.2.7 note utterance-final devoicing in such elicitation). No statement about phrase level.
new_statements.identity_note: The note is on the Waderi wordlist labelled 'Borogo na Tabaruma'; Yoder et al. 2014 code it BW 'Rogo, Waderi' = 'Borogo (Shiyabe)': Waderi people self-identify as Rogo (oRogo) but call their speech Toshiyabe; the survey and Ethnologue put 'Rogo and Shiyabe' under [rod] = Glottolog rogo1238 (no dialect sub-languoids); Blench & McGill 2012 call the unit 'Rogo-Shyabe' and note 'two types of Rogo', the other around Ucanja town (Rafi/Kusheriki LGAs). So the statement describes the Shiyabe variety of Rogo, not Ucanja Rogo proper.
